item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Repository: the tasktracker library at the repo root (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Work only in tasktracker/store.py and tests/ (read tasktracker/models.py for the task fields; do not change it unless strictly required, and say why in the commit body if you do). Add unit tests covering each acceptance bullet, including mixed LIFO sequences, undoing a delete restores the same id and fields, id non-reuse after undoing an add, and a failed complete not being undone. Keep the existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Functions stay under 60 lines and must validate inputs at the boundary; keep the undo history explicit, with no hidden shared state. Make exactly one commit on your branch with the message `TT-104: Undo`. Do not add any AI-tool attribution or co-author lines to the commit. Do not change other tickets' behaviour and add no dependencies.

model_reasons.implement: State-mutation logic with id non-reuse and LIFO history; needs careful reasoning.

pr.body: Approach: TaskStore keeps an explicit _history list of _Change records (kind, task, previous_status). add/complete/delete append only after the operation succeeds. undo() pops the last change and _revert() applies the inverse: add removes the task, complete restores the previous status (so undoing complete of an already-done task keeps it done), delete re-inserts the same Task object under the same id. _next_id is never decremented. Key files: tasktracker/store.py, tests/test_undo.py (10 new tests covering each acceptance bullet, mixed LIFO, delete restore of id and fields, id non-reuse, failed complete/delete/add not recorded). Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -> Ran 15 tests, OK. Before the change the new test module fails to import (NothingToUndo missing). models.py unchanged. Follow-ups (non-blocking): F1 delete keeps a live reference, so mutations made to the returned task before undo are restored; F2 history grows unbounded for long-lived stores; F3 consistency checks are bare asserts, stripped under python -O.
pr.summary: Made TaskStore.undo() happen. Now can revert the latest add, complete or delete, LIFO across kinds; NothingToUndo when empty. Before: no undo, now: undo walks back history; ids never reused; failed ops not recorded.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: the tasktracker library at the repo root (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Work only in tasktracker/search.py and tests/ (read tasktracker/models.py for the task fields; do not change it). Add unit tests covering each acceptance bullet. Keep the existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Functions stay under 60 lines and must validate inputs at the boundary. Make exactly one commit on your branch with the message `TT-103: Search query syntax`. Do not add any AI-tool attribution or co-author lines to the commit. Do not change other tickets' behaviour and add no dependencies.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Repository: the tasktracker library at the repo root (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Work only in tasktracker/export.py and tests/. Add unit tests covering each acceptance bullet, including titles with commas, quotes, CR and LF, and an empty task list. Keep the existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Functions stay under 60 lines and must validate inputs at the boundary. Make exactly one commit on your branch with the message `TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export`. Do not add any AI-tool attribution or co-author lines to the commit. Do not change other tickets' behaviour and add no dependencies.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Repository: the tasktracker library at the repo root (Python, standard library only). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly as written:

`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Work only in tasktracker/dates.py and tests/. Add unit tests covering each acceptance bullet. Keep the existing tests passing: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Functions stay under 60 lines and must validate inputs at the boundary. Make exactly one commit on your branch with the message `TT-101: Reject impossible due dates`. Do not add any AI-tool attribution or co-author lines to the commit. Do not change other tickets' behaviour and add no dependencies.

Offsets wrap OverflowError as InvalidDate. Inputs of wrong type raise TypeError at the boundary. Files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_dates.py (new). Checks: unittest discover, 18 tests OK. Review: pass, no blocking findings. Assumptions: TypeError for non-str/non-date input is acceptable boundary validation; no lint tool available.
pr.summary: parse_due no longer clamps impossible dates. now raises InvalidDate for 2026-02-30 and similar, and for unsupported forms. before: clamped to month end, bare ValueError; now: InvalidDate with original text.
pr.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
